2 Department of Music: BM - Music Composition: ● Replacing two portfolio classes MUS 280 and 480 with the newly approved course MUS 367 Integrative Career Studies for Musicians.
This course fulfills 3 credits of general education and serves as a D1 for this major.
The portfolio courses no longer address the needs of the students seeking careers in composition; ● deleting MUS 421 (which is only required of BM Composition majors) ● addressing changes in conducting courses for music education; composition majors will be required to take the conducting series (MUS 239 Music Gesture and Sound) and then select one of the conducting labs (MUS 311 or 312); ● adding the new course MUS 411 Advanced Performance Studies to enhance the studio lessons. ● lowering the number of required participations in ensembles to 6 semesters because of the number of required upper level theory. ● eliminating the requirement for secondary applied credits BM - Music Education: Address the gap in instruction for music education majors seeking a BM degree in music education.

Currently content addressing teaching exceptional learners and issues of inclusion are embedded in other music education courses, however, a focused course is necessary to prepare music students for a professional career in music education.
The BM degree in music education currently allows for 6 electives in music education.
This course would reduce that number of electives to 3.
The music education faculty agree that this content is essential for future music educators.
This NOC also addresses catalog errors including: ○ identifying the correct number of credits in studies in music as variable, ○ including the Unit Plan Assessment in requirements for clearance for teaching residency, ○ providing the correct EDC 484 course title, ○ providing the full and correct Praxis II test name to avoid student confusion, and ○ reflecting the minimum number of credits possible for graduation as 121.

This last item is important because combined with successfully passing piano proficiency without taking a piano class for credit and counting the possible 9 credits of MUS and 3 credits of EDC toward general education requirements students could graduate with a total of 118 credits; This is unlikely to occur, additional electives in music should be taken were that to occur COLLEGE OF BUSINESS: Management Degree: We are making these changes in a continued reimagining and reinvigoration of the Management Major and in an effort to 1) further rationalize the management major and existing tracks to streamline and support student success 2) transfer administrative ownership for the General Business Major to the Management Area as it currently has no home and 3) reinvigorate the General Business Major (which has not been reviewed or updated in more than 20 years) by combining it with management while maintaining its interdisciplinary structure within the Management major.

This will allow students to continue to combine interests across disciplines and colleges as they have done in General Business, but with more intention by following the evidence-based portfolio approach to learning while a member of a community of like-minded thinkers.
The major will streamline the process for students to double major (ie., Green Business) or earn minors in diverse areas (music, sport, theater, diversity topics) to create an academic experience that supports the individual student’s career aspirations.
